title: Building the 10-Slide Pitch Deck

slide.title: Ten Slides, One Story
slide.body: Ten small slide thumbnails in two rows of five, each showing one short line. Small tag: Building an AI Startup · Lesson 14 · Capstone step 2.

production_notes: Screen demo tool: Canva (free plan), as named in the curriculum and content.md.

[VERSION] Canva interface details must be checked against the live tool before recording: template search, slide count, style or brand options, Uploads, chart elements, Present mode, and download and share options on the free plan.
Choose a plain, generic template with no third-party brand. Olumide's MVP screenshots are mock-ups with fake data; no real pharmacy names or customer data on screen.

Olumide (Ibadan, Nigeria) is fictional; '11 interviews, 34 of 120 visitors (threshold 25), 4 pharmacies in a paid pilot' are part of the example, not statistics. The chart on slide 6 uses placeholder numbers.
Record at 1080p and zoom to about 150% when typing slide titles so the text is readable.

Hook.voiceover: A person reading your deck may give each slide only a few seconds. If a slide tries to say five things, they will remember none. If each slide says one thing clearly, they can follow your whole story in minutes.

Explain.voiceover: In the last lesson, you recorded your demo. Now, capstone step two. A pitch deck is a short set of slides that explains your business. The rule for every slide is one message. Write that message as the slide title, as a full sentence, and use the rest of the slide to support it.

slide.title: Building the 10-Slide Pitch Deck
slide.body: Building an AI Startup · Lesson 14 of 15 · Capstone step 2

Explain.voiceover: Here is the outline. Problem, solution, and a demo with screenshots. Then customer evidence: interviews, your demand test and any pilots. Then market: the first customers you can realistically reach, calculated from the bottom up, so you can explain every number.

slide.title: Slides 1 to 5
slide.body: 1. Problem · 2. Solution · 3. Demo · 4. Customer evidence · 5. Market (bottom up: shops in our city × share we can reach)

Explain.voiceover: Then business model, with your margin and your plan for heavy users. Moat, where you are honest that the model itself is not the moat. Competition, including spreadsheets, manual work and general AI chat apps. Team. And finally the ask: exactly what you want from this audience.

slide.title: Slides 6 to 10
slide.body: 6. Business model · 7. Moat (not the model) · 8. Competition (incl. spreadsheets, manual work, chat apps) · 9. Team · 10. The ask

Explain.voiceover: Keep the text short, use large fonts and simple visuals. And keep your risk checklist and unit economics sheet ready as backup, because good questions will come after the last slide.
Explain.on_screen_text: Short text. Large fonts. Backup ready.

Explain.voiceover: A pitch deck is like road signs on a motorway. Each sign gives one piece of information, large and clear, because drivers see it only for a moment. A sign with a paragraph of text would be useless.
Explain.stock_query: large road signs over busy motorway

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's build one. Olumide is a made up founder in Ibadan, Nigeria. His MVP helps pharmacies check stock and expiry dates by reading photos of shelves and invoices. We build his deck in Canva. The menus may look a little different when you try it, but the steps are the same.

slide.title: Olumide's startup
slide.body: 'Pharmacies check stock and expiry dates from photos of shelves and invoices.' Caption: Olumide · Ibadan · made up founder

Demonstrate.voiceover: We open Canva with a free account, search for pitch deck, and choose a simple template with plenty of white space. Then we set it to exactly ten slides, deleting or duplicating slides as needed.
screen_steps: Open Canva and sign in with a free account.
Type 'pitch deck' in the search bar and filter to Presentations [VERSION].
Choose a simple template with plenty of white space.
In the page view, delete extra slides or duplicate slides until there are exactly 10.

Demonstrate.voiceover: Next, we apply the brand colours and font once, so every slide matches. Then we write all the slide titles first. For slide one, small pharmacies lose stock to expiry because they track dates on paper.
screen_steps: Open the template's style or brand options and apply one colour set and one font to all pages [VERSION].
Click the title on slide 1 and type: 'Small pharmacies lose stock to expiry because they track dates on paper.'
Scroll through slides 2 to 10 and type a full-sentence title on each.

Demonstrate.voiceover: On slide four, we add the evidence. Eleven interviews. A waitlist of thirty four out of one hundred and twenty visitors, against a threshold of twenty five. And four pharmacies in a paid pilot.
screen_steps: Go to slide 4 and add a text box.
Type: '11 interviews · waitlist 34 of 120 visitors (threshold 25) · 4 pharmacies in a paid pilot'.
Increase the font size so the three numbers are easy to read.

Demonstrate.voiceover: On slide three, we add screenshots from the MVP with the uploads option. First, we check that they contain no real customer data. On slide six, we add a simple chart of revenue and cost to serve for a typical customer.
screen_steps: Open Uploads and upload two MVP screenshots made with fake data [VERSION].
Drag them onto slide 3 and align them side by side.
Go to slide 6, open Elements, search 'chart' and insert a bar chart [VERSION].
Edit the chart data to two bars: revenue and cost to serve for a typical customer (placeholder numbers).

Demonstrate.voiceover: Now a check. The first draft of slide seven said, we use the latest AI. That is not a moat. So we change it: a growing set of corrected shelf photos from partner pharmacies, used with permission, and a distribution deal with a pharmacists' association.
screen_steps: Go to slide 7 and highlight the title 'We use the latest AI'.
Replace it with: 'Our moat: a growing set of corrected shelf photos from partner pharmacies, used with permission, and a distribution deal with a pharmacists' association.'
Shorten the supporting text to two lines.

Demonstrate.voiceover: Finally, we use present mode to read through the whole deck, checking that each slide has one message. Then we download it as a PDF, or share a view only link.
screen_steps: Click Present and step through all 10 slides [VERSION].
Exit, click Share, then Download and choose PDF [VERSION].
Show the alternative: create a view-only link.

Demonstrate.voiceover: A common mistake is filling slides with long sentences and reading them aloud. Another is using a large market number from the internet that you cannot explain. Use a small, realistic number you can defend. And never skip the ask. Every pitch should end with a clear request, such as a pilot, an introduction or a specific investment.

slide.title: Common mistakes
slide.body: Red crosses: long sentences read aloud · a huge unexplained market number · no ask. Green ticks: short titles · a small number you can defend · a clear request.

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, use ten slides: problem, solution, demo, evidence, market, business model, moat, competition, team and the ask. Second, give every slide one message, written as a full sentence title. Third, use your own evidence and unit economics, and keep backup detail ready for questions.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Ten slides, from problem to ask. 2. One message per slide, full-sentence title. 3. Your own evidence; backup ready.

CTA.voiceover: Now it is your turn. This is capstone step two. In the exercise below this video, build your ten slide pitch deck in Canva, using your validation evidence and unit economics. Check that slide seven describes a real moat and slide ten has a clear ask. Next, and last, we look at pitching to customers and investors. See you there.
